setup: python and python3 can point to different installs — verify both.
Pick an exact version instead of fighting PATH.

py -3.12 script.py
py -0p   # list installed versions
One project, one environment — never pip install globally.
Old pip fails on new wheels with cryptic errors.
Reproducible setups beat "works on my machine".

pip install requests
pip freeze > requirements.txt
pip install -r requirements.txt
Runs from the right directory, no path hacks.
help, dir and type answer most "what is this?" questions.
Handy in the REPL for quick follow-up math.

# Ctrl+L clears the screen
# exit() or Ctrl+Z then Enter quits
See versions and locations when imports misbehave.

pip show requests
pip list --outdated
python -m site
syntax: Four spaces per level; never mix tabs and spaces.
snake_case for functions, SHOUTING for constants.
Reads like maths, no and needed.
Empty values are False — use that instead of len() checks.

if items:          # [] "" 0 None are all False
    print("has data")
if name.strip():
    print("not blank")

a, b = b, a
first, *rest = [1, 2, 3, 4]
# rest == [2, 3, 4]
Capture a value while testing it (3.8+).
One statement per line is the house style.
Hints document intent; check them with mypy.

def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"hi {name}"
strings: Prefix with f and drop variables straight in.
{x=} prints name and value — perfect for debugging.
Commas, decimals and percents without helpers.
Plus copies the string every time; join does one pass.

parts = []
for u in users:
    parts.append(u.name)
text = "\n".join(parts)
rsplit with maxsplit peels off extensions and tails.
strip cleans both ends; lstrip/rstrip pick a side.
Third argument caps how many get swapped.
Zero-pad IDs and counters in one call.
Raw strings for paths and regex
Lower() misses some Unicode; casefold does not.
Keep SQL/HTML readable without stray spaces.

import textwrap
q = textwrap.dedent("""
    SELECT * FROM users
    WHERE active = 1
""")
collections: Build lists in one readable line.

squares = [x * x for x in range(10)]
names = [u["name"] for u in users]

evens = [x for x in nums if x % 2 == 0]
clean = [s.strip() for s in lines if s.strip()]

lengths = {w: len(w) for w in words}
remainders = {x % 3 for x in nums}

for i, name in enumerate(names, start=1):
    print(f"{i}. {name}")
Pair lists safely; strict=True shouts on mismatch.

for k, v in zip(keys, vals, strict=True):
    print(k, v)
Grab the ends, keep the middle.
Append to a list that may not exist yet.
Three lines of tallying become one.

from collections import defaultdict
by_team = defaultdict(list)
by_team["a"].append("ana")
A rolling window that forgets old items itself.

from collections import deque
last5 = deque(maxlen=5)
for x in stream:
    last5.append(x)
Sort by any attribute, forward or back.

by_age = sorted(users, key=lambda u: u["age"])
by_score = sorted(users, key=lambda u: u["score"], reverse=True)

items[::-1]       # reversed copy
top3 = scores[:3]
without_first = items[1:]
any and all read like English
Short-circuit: they stop at the first answer.
functions: *args and **kwargs
Accept any extras and forward them.
Never use a mutable default
One shared list surprises every caller — default to None.

def add(item, box=None):
    box = box if box is not None else []
    box.append(item)
    return box
Keyword-only arguments
Force clarity at call sites with a bare *.
Lambdas shine as keys
Tiny throwaway functions for sort/max/min.

max(users, key=lambda u: u["score"])
sorted(names, key=lambda n: len(n))
Cache pure functions
lru_cache memoizes expensive repeats for free.
Closures make factories
Inner function remembers the outer argument.

def make_greeter(word):
    return lambda name: f"{word}, {name}"
hi = make_greeter("hello")
hi("ana")
Write docstrings
Triple-quoted first line powers help().
Return tuples freely
Multiple values come back as one tuple.
next with a default
Find-or-None without try/except.
admin = next((u for u in users if u["role"] == "admin"), None)
Generators beat lists in any/all
No temporary list — stops at first match.

if any(u["banned"] for u in users):
    print("review needed")
oop: self is the instance being built.
Init, repr and equality generated for you.
Call it like data, compute it like code.
Reuse the parent init, then add yours.
Fixed fields, no per-instance dict — for millions of objects.
Subclasses must implement the abstract method.
files: No close() to forget, even on errors.

with open("notes.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    text = f.read()

from pathlib import Path
p = Path("data") / "in.csv"
if p.exists():
    print(p.stat().st_size)

import csv
with open("users.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        print(row["email"])
Stream big files line by line
a mode creates the file if missing.

with open("app.log", "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("started\n")
errors: Bare except hides bugs — name the failure.
Keep the original cause in the traceback.
Callers can catch YOUR failure precisely.
Levels, timestamps and files for free.

import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logging.info("started for %s", user)
Last line names the error; top shows the path.

from datetime import datetime
now = datetime.now()
print(now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"))

from datetime import date, timedelta
deadline = date.today() + timedelta(days=7)

random.choice(["a", "b", "c"])
random.shuffle(deck)

import secrets
token = secrets.token_hex(16)
code = secrets.randbelow(9000) + 1000

reduce(lambda a, b: a + b, [1, 2, 3])
double = partial(lambda f, x: f * x, 2)

from collections import namedtuple
Point = namedtuple("Point", "x y")
p = Point(1, 2)
print(p.x)

prod: Import-safe modules run tests without side effects.
Values on demand, not a billion-item list.

total = sum(x * x for x in range(10 ** 9))

import sys
sys.getsizeof([1] * 1000)       # ~8KB
sys.getsizeof(x for x in range(1000))  # ~200B
